stories.title: TEST STORY: why reusable rockets made space cheaper
stories.angle: Landing rockets instead of throwing them away changed the cost of space

scenes.text: For sixty years, every rocket we launched was thrown away after one flight.
Imagine flying a plane across the ocean, then scrapping it on landing.
That's why getting anything into space cost a fortune.
But here's the part that matters: rockets can now land themselves and fly again.
Reuse the hardware, and the price of every launch drops.
Would you ride a rocket that has already flown ten times? Because for sixty years, every rocket was thrown away.

intro.text: One of these ideas sounds like science fiction, and it's already happening.
Here are two tech stories, counting down to the biggest one.

scenes.text: Number two. Walk into a modern warehouse and you might see more robots than people.
Small machines carry whole shelves to human workers, so nobody walks miles a day.
It's faster, and it changes what warehouse jobs look like.
But the next story goes much higher. Literally.
Number one. For decades, every rocket was used once and thrown away.
Now some rockets land upright, get checked, and fly again.
Reusing them is a big reason launch prices have dropped.

outro.text: So which one surprised you more? Tell me in the comments.
